note: Discovery leads for sociology topic workers (phase 4). LITERACY level: general. NO policy positions; NO political advocacy; contested concepts (race, gender, inequality) taught descriptively with attributed sources. All examples ORIGINAL (fictional people/scenarios). Tier A anchors: OpenStax Introduction to Sociology 3e (openstax.org blocks direct fetch → Wayback captures of canonical URLs; the LibreTexts mirror works too), American Sociological Association (asanet.org), Pew Research Center (pewresearch.org — live, excellent for factual social data), U.S. Census Bureau (census.gov — live), Bureau of Labor Statistics (bls.gov), Statista (Tier C — avoid unless nothing else). Tier B: Britannica, Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy (for theory). Registry check FIRST: sociology sibling content may exist in phase-3 (check content/phase-2/source-registry.json AND content/phase-3 subject workspaces — sociology appeared in earlier phases); openstax-intro-sociology ids may exist. Reuse identical URLs.
cautions: Culture/norms/values: teach descriptively (what sociologists mean by these terms); no moral ranking of cultures.
Social stratification/class/poverty: factual framing with attributed data (Census, Pew, BLS); no policy prescriptions.
Race and ethnicity: define as social constructs per mainstream sociology (ASA/OpenStax); no biological claims; no policy positions.
Gender: descriptive sociology (sex vs gender distinction per ASA/OpenStax); no advocacy.
Family/religion/work/economy/politics/media: descriptive institutions; no political endorsements; religion described as a social institution, not evaluated.
Crime and deviance: sociological theories (labeling, strain) attributed; no fear-mongering; U.S. data from BJS (bjs.ojp.gov) attributed.
